title: A save file from samples
description:
A small game the course provides writes save files in an undocumented format. You made it save four times with controlled changes (lesson 6.02):

```text
A  the start of a game: player "Ada", level 3, standing at x 100, y -2.5, carrying 5 of item 7
   53 41 56 45 02 00 03 41 64 61 03 00 00 00 C8 42 00 00 20 C0 01 07 00 05 34 04 00 00
B  the same, after renaming the player to "Adam"
   53 41 56 45 02 00 04 41 64 61 6D 03 00 00 00 C8 42 00 00 20 C0 01 07 00 05 A2 04 00 00
C  A, after picking up 1 of item 300
   53 41 56 45 02 00 03 41 64 61 03 00 00 00 C8 42 00 00 20 C0 02 07 00 05 2C 01 01 63 04 00 00
D  A, after levelling up to 4 and moving to x 101
   53 41 56 45 02 00 03 41 64 61 04 00 00 00 CA 42 00 00 20 C0 01 07 00 05 37 04 00 00
```

Your notes so far:
- The file always starts `53 41 56 45`, then `02 00` in every sample.
- The name's bytes are preceded by a byte that equals its length.
- The last four bytes change whenever anything changes. Adding up every byte before them gives the same number.
- Floats are 4 bytes, little-endian (`00 00 C8 42` is 100.0).

Work out the rest from the samples, then write a reader and a writer:

```cpp
struct Item { std::uint16_t id; std::uint8_t quantity; };
struct Save { std::string name; std::uint16_t level; float x, y; std::vector<Item> items; };

std::optional<Save> parseSave(const std::vector<std::uint8_t>& file);
std::vector<std::uint8_t> writeSave(const Save& save);
```

**parseSave** returns `std::nullopt` for a file with the wrong magic, a version other than 2, a wrong checksum, too few bytes for what the header announces, or bytes left over after the checksum. **writeSave** produces exactly the bytes the game would.
hints: Compare A with D: two bytes right after the name changed from `03 00` to `04 00` (the level), and four bytes after that are the x position. Compare A with C: the byte after the floats went from 1 to 2, and three bytes were added before the checksum: `2C 01 01`.
Read with a moving offset and check that enough bytes remain before every read. For the writer, build every byte except the checksum, add them up, and append the sum as 4 little-endian bytes.
